title: A spoken turn's failure and ADR 0110's ended-utterance sentences never reach her window
body:
## Summary
The voice store writes why a spoken turn ended or failed into `useVoice.reason`, and nothing in her window or the halo reads it; only the Setup and Mind rows do.

## Description
apps/desktop/src/stores/voice.ts:267 (an ended utterance: too_short, silent with its dB, no_words), :309 (turn.error) and :455 (the socket closing mid-turn) set `reason` and move the phase to idle or error. Her window's model takes only `phase`, `available` and `partial` from the voice store (apps/desktop/src/companion/model.ts:113-118 PanelVoice; companion/live.tsx:149,182,190 read `phase`), and the halo's caption reads `partial`, `speakingText` and `heard` (apps/desktop/src/lib/halo.ts:79-84). The reason is read by modules/setup/index.ts:52 and the Mind depth's Voice card alone. docs/adr/0110-a-heard-utterance-ends-in-a-named-outcome.md:50 gives each outcome its own sentence and promises (Consequences) that 'a muted or misrouted microphone reports the level it measured instead of saying nothing' - at the surface where the key was pressed, it still says nothing: the halo goes dark and her window returns to rest. Technique: voice-io/voice-ux-integration ('degraded affordances tell one honest sentence'). Fixed looks like: her window (talk tab or caption) and/or the halo show the store's reason for a few seconds after a spoken turn ends without a reply, with a plain sentence for a turn.error (companion/plain.ts plainFailure).

## Flow
- hold the chord with a muted microphone and let go
- the daemon answers voice.transcript final, outcome silent, peak_dbfs -70
- stores/voice.ts:267 sets phase idle, reason 'your microphone sounded silent (-70 dB), check the input in Voice settings'
- her window and the halo read only the phase: the halo goes dark, nothing is said; the sentence is visible only if the person opens Setup or Mind
- fix order: a test in companion/model.test.ts feeding PanelVoice a reason; add `reason` to PanelVoice; render it where the spoken turn lives (her caption/talk), plainFailure for turn.error codes

## Expected impact
Everyone who uses push-to-talk and gets no answer: today a silent mic, a tap, a 'no words' and an engine failure all look identical (nothing happens). Measured as outcome sentences rendered in her window: 0 of 4 today. What could break: a reason that lingers past the next press; it must clear on press as the store already does (stores/voice.ts:498).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the four ways a spoken turn ends without a reply each say their sentence where the key was pressed
Before: 0 of 4 outcomes (too_short, silent, no_words, turn.error) reach her window or the halo; PanelVoice has no reason field (companion/model.ts:113-118)
After: 4 of 4, by a companion model test that feeds each reason (predicted; not built - the render lives in companion/, outside this round's paths)
Method: simulation - the four outcomes walked through stores/voice.ts and companion/model.ts; the rung above needs an edit to companion/ (desktop-companion context)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: companion/model.test.ts: build the panel model with voice {phase: idle, reason: <each of the 4 sentences>} after a press; count how many reach a rendered caption/talk line (before 0/4, after 4/4); plus a halo captionOf case.

title: Voice failures reach the person as reason codes and browser messages
body:
## Summary
Four voice surfaces print the daemon's closed reason vocabulary and the webview's own error text verbatim, where companion/plain.ts exists to turn them into sentences.

## Description
apps/desktop/src/stores/voice.ts:309 stores a turn.error as `${event.reason}: ${event.detail}` (e.g. 'engine_error: ...'), shown on Setup's voice row (modules/setup/index.ts:52). apps/desktop/src/modules/voice/live.ts:174 (problem), :209, :351, :359 (saveError) write `${out.reason}: ${refusalText(out)}`; with the daemon unreachable that reads 'daemon_offline: Failed to fetch' (refusalText returns the fetch error's message before its own 'the daemon did not answer', lib/voice-setup.ts:145-160). apps/desktop/src/companion/plain.ts:1-8 states the house rule - 'a person should never have to read it ... No sentence here may use ... engine_error' - and the typed turn honours it (companion/model.ts:620 plainFailure). The spoken turn and the Voice module do not. Note: the scenes card 'A key refusal is shown under the Listener row' (desktop-scenes-voice-waking) is about WHERE saveError shows; this card is about WHAT it says. modules/voice/fixtures.ts:183 pins the code-prefixed form ('validator_failed: the key does not look like an OpenAI key'), so the fix changes a fixture too.

## Flow
- stop the daemon while the Voice settings are open and press Save key
- lib/voice-setup.ts send() catches TypeError 'Failed to fetch' -> refusal offline, reason daemon_offline, detail 'Failed to fetch'
- live.ts:351 sets saveError 'daemon_offline: Failed to fetch'
- fix order: one voice sentence helper (refusal -> sentence, reusing plainFailure's words for turn.error), applied at the four sites; fixtures and tests updated

## Expected impact
Anyone who meets a voice failure reads a sentence instead of a code. Measured as shown strings that start with an ERROR_REASONS code: 4 sites today, 0 after. What could break: a test or fixture that pins today's prefixed text (fixtures.ts:183, live.test.ts).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a voice failure reads as a sentence, not a reason code or 'Failed to fetch'
Before: 4 sites print `<code>: <detail>` (stores/voice.ts:309, live.ts:174,209,351/359)
After: 0 (predicted; plainFailure lives in companion/, and importing it into stores/ is a layering call this round did not make)
Method: simulation - the offline save walked through send/refusalText/saveKey; the rung above needs companion/plain.ts or a shared lib home for its words
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: A test over the four sites (stores/voice turn.error, live.ts problem/saveError for offline and invalid) asserting the shown string does not start with any ERROR_REASONS member and is not the bare fetch message; before 4 fail, after 0.

title: The manual-install links open with target=_blank from the chrome webview, unseen
body:
## Summary
The Kokoro manual-install card links to the sherpa-onnx release pages with `target="_blank"`, and nothing in the shell is known to route a new-window request from the chrome webview to the system browser.

## Description
apps/desktop/src/modules/voice/parts.tsx:113 renders MANUAL_LINKS (modules/voice/model.ts:298-304) as `<a target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">`. The shell grants new windows only to tab webviews (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/tabs.rs:237 `.on_new_window(... Allow)`); for the chrome webview the WebView2 default for an unhandled new-window request is a bare popup window, or nothing, depending on configuration. scenes/accounts/view.tsx:711 uses the same pattern for an OAuth link, so whatever is true is true twice. This is the one place in the voice studio where the person must leave the app (the 'manual' install case), so a link that opens nothing strands them. Fixed looks like: links go through the shell's opener (or a tab), once someone has seen what happens today.

## Flow
- an install the daemon answers `manual` (no network installer for this platform)
- the studio's install card shows the two links and Check again
- the person clicks 'sherpa-onnx v1.13.4 (the engine)'
- observed: unknown - needs the real Tauri window on Windows to see whether a popup, the browser, or nothing appears

## Expected impact
People on the manual path only; if the link opens nothing, they cannot finish voice setup at all. What could break: nothing until a fix is chosen.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the manual install's links reach a browser
Before: unknown (no test, no shell handler for the chrome webview's new-window requests found by grep)
After: unknown
Method: simulation - grep of the shell for new-window handling; the rung above needs the real window, which this round cannot drive
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/desktop/src/modules/voice/parts.tsx:113  <a className="typo-body" href={link.href} target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">
apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/tabs.rs:237  .on_new_window(|_url, _features| tauri::webview::NewWindowResponse::Allow)   (tab webviews)
$ grep -rn "openUrl\|opener\|open_external" apps/desktop/src --include=*.ts* | grep -v test -> (none)
apps/desktop/src/scenes/accounts/view.tsx:711  same target="_blank" pattern

title: Both voice players keep their AudioContext running after the last sound
body:
## Summary
The studio's preview player and her reply player each create one AudioContext and never suspend or close it, so after the first preview or reply the webview's audio render thread runs for the rest of the window's life.

## Description
apps/desktop/src/modules/voice/audio.ts:26 PreviewPlayer creates its context on the first play and only `close()` (audio.ts:82) releases it; `close()` has no production caller. apps/desktop/src/lib/voice.ts Player creates its context on her first chunk and has no close or suspend at all; the store drops the Player reference on close() (stores/voice.ts:568) without closing its context. A running AudioContext keeps the audio device open and the render thread ticking; suspend() on the last source's end, and resume() on the next play (both players now resume a suspended context), would idle it. Whether the idle cost is worth a line in this app is a measurement nobody has taken.

## Flow
- open the Voice studio and play one preview (or speak one turn)
- the clip ends; the context stays 'running'
- measure: the webview process's idle CPU and the audio render thread in Task Manager / chrome://media-internals, before and after suspend-on-idle

## Expected impact
Battery and idle CPU of a desktop app that sits open all day. Measured as the context state after the last clip: running today, suspended after. What could break: the first chunk after a suspend must resume first (both players now do), or the head of a reply is clipped.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - no audio render thread spins while nothing plays
Before: context.state stays 'running' after the last clip (both players; no suspend call exists: grep)
After: 'suspended' after the last source ends (predicted)
Method: simulation - the state can be probed with a fake context, but the claim is idle CPU, which needs the real window
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
$ grep -rn "\.suspend(" apps/desktop/src --include=*.ts* -> (none)
$ grep -rn "\.close()" apps/desktop/src --include=*.ts* | grep -v test -> lib/voice.ts:249,263 (socket), :333 (microphone) - no player context close
apps/desktop/src/modules/voice/audio.ts:82-87  close() { ... void this.context?.close(); }   (0 production callers)
apps/desktop/src/stores/voice.ts:568  player = null;   (its context is never closed)
